title: Sh-M-R
hookLine: shamar: guard, keep, observe, as in keeping Shabbat

cards: "Am I my brother's keeper?" It's a dodge. God has just asked Cain where his brother Abel is, and Cain, who knows exactly where Abel is lying, answers with a shrug turned into a question.
In the King James it runs: "I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?" People still quote that line when they mean not my problem. But listen to the noun he picks.
Keeper. In Hebrew, shomer: the one who guards, the one who keeps watch. Cain reaches for that word only to push it away.
Today's root is the word he wouldn't take on.

teach.h: TO DRESS IT AND TO KEEP IT.
teach.b: Sh-M-R. Shin, mem, resh. Guard, keep, watch, observe: English needs several words for one Hebrew root.
Turn it four ways. First, the garden. God puts the human in Eden "to dress it and to keep it."
Keep is shamar. The job handed over in Eden is guarding something that isn't theirs. Hold on to dress it, too; tomorrow's root is hiding there.
Second, Cain. Two chapters later, the same job comes back as a refusal.

teach.h: CAIN REFUSES TO BE A KEEPER.
teach.b: The garden had a keeper; Cain won't be one for his own brother. God doesn't argue the point. The next words are about Abel's blood, crying out from the ground.
The story answers the question. Third, God as keeper.

teach.h: THE LORD BLESS THEE, AND KEEP THEE.
teach.b: The priestly blessing opens: "The LORD bless thee, and keep thee." And a psalm promises, "he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep." The role Cain wouldn't touch, God takes on, without a night off.
When Deuteronomy repeats the Ten Commandments, the Sabbath line opens with shamor, keep, and a Jew who observes Shabbat is called shomer Shabbat, a Sabbath keeper.
Put the four together and keeping looks less like storing something in a drawer and more like a watchman on a city wall at night. Whatever you keep, you also have to watch.

how: Jews who observe the Sabbath are called shomer Shabbat, Sabbath keepers; the priestly blessing, which opens 'the LORD bless thee, and keep thee', is said in synagogue and by parents over children on Friday night.

s: the first job given in Eden was to rule the garden
"to dress it and to keep it": keep is shamar.
the same root covers guarding a garden and keeping the Sabbath
the word Cain uses for keeper, shomer, comes from the same root as keeping the garden
shamar: keep the garden; shomer: the keeper.

games.q: you're Cain. God asks you where your brother Abel is. what do you say?
o: I know not: am I my brother's keeper?
let me go and look for him.
games.why: "I know not: Am I my brother's keeper?" he reaches for shomer, keeper, only to refuse it.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you've said you'd do, the smallest one that's slipping: call your mother back, return the borrowed book, finish what you told a coworker you'd finish.
Picture the exact moment you'll keep it, where you'll be and the first words you'll say, and guard that moment the way a watchman guards a gate. If you pray, you can ask for help keeping it.

wordCard.voice: Sh-M-R. Shin, mem, resh: shamar, to keep and guard; shomer, the keeper. The garden, the brother, the blessing, the Sabbath. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: he kept, he guarded, he watched.

carryVoice: Your line: keep and guard. Keeping, in this root, means watching over. That's today, done.
